messages.author: 750b640c36dea72c
messages.subject: traceplot thinning problems
parts:
Hi Stan,

I'm pretty new at Stan and I bumped into a graphical problem concerning traceplots in Stan.
With these options:

nchains <- 1;
niter <- 15000;
nwarmup <- 5000;
thin<-3;

I run my model in R,having my stan object, and I want to do the traceplots of some parameters with this command:

traceplot(fit12, "beta_look", inc_warmup = F,ask=T)

However, when visualising them, all the 15000 iterations appear and not only (15000/thin) iterations,as I expect to obtain from Jags.
Are there any options to include in the traceplot command? I read the manual but I don't find anything

Thank you very much,
Luke

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] traceplot thinning problems
parts:
Thinning still happens, but the labels on the x axis
indicate the unthinned positions.

For example, if I run this:

> fit <- stan(model_code="parameters { real y; } model { y ~ normal(0,1); }", thin = 100, chains=1)

Then it'll show 0 to 2000 on the x axis, but you can clearly
see that there are only 20 draws being plotted.

I sort of like seeing the original position of the draws, but
I certainly see how it's confusing.

I'm not sure what the right thing to do here is.

- Bob
